songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: Soaring Dark Star medley, electric St. Stephen > Lovelight, tight jam flow
ai_show_review.blurb: The show shines with a soaring Dark Star that segues into Mountains of the Moon and a blistering Saint Stephen → Turn On Your Lovelight transition. Garcia’s guitar is on fire, Phil drives the rhythm, and the dual drummers create a six‑armed groove. Highlights include Dupree's Diamond Blues, The Eleven, Alligator and Pigpen’s raw Hard To Handle.
ai_show_review.review: On April 5, 1969 at San Francisco’s Avalon Ballroom the Dead delivered one of their most psychedelic arcs. Opening acoustic with Dupree's Diamond Blues, they launched into a Mountains Of The Moon → Dark Star journey that showcases Jerry Garcia’s flawless tone and aggressive soloing, while Phil Lesh’s bass underpins the entire medley. The set then rockets through Saint Stephen into an electric Turn On Your Lovelight, followed by The Eleven with its signature time‑signature twist. In the second set Pigpen’s gritty vocals on Hard To Handle add raw energy before the band dives deep into China Cat Sunflower, a double Cryptical Envelopment / The Other One suite, and a marathon Alligator jam that segues into drums, feedback and a gentle good night. Across three pristine soundboard captures the performance feels locked‑in; the “six‑armed” drumming of Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann fuels every transition, and Tom Constanten’s piano adds a carousel‑like swirl to the acoustic numbers. This show is a must‑listen for anyone craving the early Dead’s exploratory spirit.

best_recording.reason: Pristine soundboard capture with excellent tape clarity, full set and the most frequently cited standout moments.

key_highlights: Soaring Dark Star → Mountains Of The Moon segues with pristine guitar tone.
Electric Saint Stephen → Turn On Your Lovelight transition is blistering.
Marathon jam stretch Dark Star → Saint Stephen → Love Light showcases peak improvisation.
Dual‑drummer “six‑armed” rhythm section drives the set’s momentum.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is on fire, delivering perfect tone on Dark Star, aggressive solos throughout, expressive acoustic work on Dupree's/Mountains and slide flair on Hard To Handle.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides a solid, driving bass foundation, especially powering the Dark Star medley and maintaining tight groove; his interplay with the two drummers is noted as ‘six‑armed’.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s vocals show early cracks, particularly on Hard To Handle, but his rhythm work fits the evolving sound; overall still developing.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart’s drumming blends with Bill’s, forming a six‑armed rhythm machine that drives the jams.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann adds tight, propulsive beats and fluid fills, complementing Hart’s power.

must_listen_sequences: And We Bid You Good Night
